title: Job Chapter 39 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Job chapter 39 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Job Chapter 39 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Job Chapter 39.

questions.question: In Job 39, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Knowest thou the time when the wild goats of the rock bring forth?
Who hath sent out the wild ass free?
Will the unicorn be willing to serve thee?
Canst thou bind the unicorn with his band in the furrow?
questions.correctAnswer: Knowest thou the time when the wild goats of the rock bring forth?
questions.explanation: This appears first in the chapter as it is the first verse of Job 39.

questions.question: What does Job 39:2 ask about the wild goats?
options: Canst thou number the months that they fulfil?
Canst thou bind the unicorn with his band in the furrow?
Will the unicorn be willing to serve thee?
Knowest thou the time when they bring forth?
questions.correctAnswer: Canst thou number the months that they fulfil?
questions.explanation: This question is directly stated in Job 39:2.

questions.question: What do the wild goats do when they bring forth their young ones according to Job 39:3?
options: They scorn the multitude of the city.
questions.explanation: This is stated in Job 39:3, describing the behavior of the wild goats.

questions.question: According to Job 39:4, how are the young ones of the wild goats described?
options: They grow up in the city.
They are scorned by the driver.
questions.explanation: Job 39:4 states that their young ones are in good liking.

questions.question: What has been made the dwelling of the wild ass according to Job 39:6?
questions.explanation: Job 39:6 states that the wilderness is the house made for the wild ass.

questions.question: What does the wild ass scorn according to Job 39:7?
questions.explanation: Job 39:7 indicates that the wild ass scorneth the multitude of the city.

questions.question: Where does the wild ass search for food according to Job 39:8?
questions.explanation: Job 39:8 states that the wild ass searcheth after every green thing.

questions.question: What is asked about the unicorn in Job 39:9?
options: Will he abide by thy crib?
Will he search for green things?
questions.correctAnswer: Will he abide by thy crib?
questions.explanation: Job 39:9 poses the question about whether the unicorn will abide by thy crib.

questions.question: What does Job 39:10 ask about binding the unicorn?
options: Canst thou bind the unicorn with his band in the furrow?
Canst thou number the months they fulfil?
Will he grow up with corn?
questions.correctAnswer: Canst thou bind the unicorn with his band in the furrow?
questions.explanation: This question is directly stated in Job 39:10.

questions.question: According to Job 39:5, who hath sent out the wild ass free?
options: Who hath loosed the bands of the wild ass?
questions.correctAnswer: Who hath loosed the bands of the wild ass?
questions.explanation: This is stated directly in Job 39:5, questioning who has loosed the bands of the wild ass.

questions.question: In Job 39:4, what happens to the young ones of the wild goats?
questions.explanation: Job 39:4 mentions that the young ones grow up with corn.

questions.question: True or False: The wild ass does not regard the crying of the driver.
questions.explanation: Job 39:7 states that the wild ass neither regardeth he the crying of the driver.

questions.question: True or False: The unicorn is described as being willing to serve.
questions.explanation: Job 39:9 poses the question of whether the unicorn will be willing to serve.

questions.question: True or False: The wild goats are said to live in the city.
questions.explanation: The text does not say that wild goats live in the city; they are associated with the wilderness.

questions.question: True or False: The wild ass is known for its willingness to serve humans.
questions.explanation: The text does not say that the wild ass is willing to serve humans; it scorns the city.

medium.title: Job Chapter 39 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Job Chapter 39 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Wilt thou trust him, because his strength is great?
questions.explanation: The question challenges the reader to consider whether to trust in God's strength, as stated in Job 39:11.

questions.question: What does Job 39:12 promise will happen if someone believes God will bring home their seed?
questions.explanation: Job 39:12 suggests that trust in God's provision leads to successful harvests, implying a reward for faith.

questions.question: What does Job 39:13 refer to regarding the peacocks?
questions.explanation: Job 39:13 speaks specifically about the goodly wings given to peacocks, highlighting their beauty.

questions.question: What does Job 39:14 indicate about the ostrich's behavior towards her eggs?
options: She leaves them in the earth
questions.correctAnswer: She leaves them in the earth
questions.explanation: Job 39:14 states that the ostrich leaves her eggs in the earth and warms them in dust, showing neglect.

questions.question: What does Job 39:15 reveal about the ostrich's concern for her eggs?
options: She forgets that they can be crushed
questions.correctAnswer: She forgets that they can be crushed
questions.explanation: Job 39:15 indicates that the ostrich forgets about dangers to her eggs, showing a lack of instinctual care.

questions.question: According to Job 39:16, how does the ostrich behave towards her young?
questions.explanation: Job 39:16 explains that the ostrich is unfeeling towards her young, indicating a lack of maternal instinct.

questions.question: What does Job 39:17 imply about the ostrich's wisdom?
questions.explanation: Job 39:17 states that God has deprived the ostrich of wisdom and understanding, affecting her behavior.

questions.question: What does Job 39:18 say about the ostrich compared to a horse and rider?
questions.explanation: Job 39:18 indicates that when she lifts herself high, she looks down on the horse and his rider, showing her pride.

questions.question: Job 39:19 asks if anyone has given strength to which animal?
questions.explanation: Job 39:19 specifically inquires about whether God has given strength to the horse, emphasizing its power.

questions.question: What does Job 39:20 question about the horse?
options: If it can be made afraid
If it can carry a rider
questions.correctAnswer: If it can be made afraid
questions.explanation: Job 39:20 poses the question of whether one can make the horse afraid, highlighting its brave nature.

questions.question: How can we relate the themes of Job 39 to our faith in God's strength?
options: By relying on our own strength
questions.explanation: The verses discuss the strength and wisdom of God in creation, encouraging us to trust Him in our lives.

questions.question: How does the behavior of the ostrich reflect on our responsibilities as Christians?
options: We must protect what is valuable
questions.correctAnswer: We must protect what is valuable
questions.explanation: The ostrich's neglect of her eggs illustrates the need for vigilance and care in our responsibilities.

questions.question: True or False: The horse is described as having a fearful nature in Job 39.
questions.explanation: Job 39:20 suggests that the horse is not afraid, which indicates its brave nature.

questions.question: True or False: The ostrich is known for its wisdom according to Job 39.
questions.explanation: Job 39:17 explicitly states that God has deprived the ostrich of wisdom.

questions.question: True or False: Job 39 encourages us to trust in God's strength and provision.
questions.explanation: The overall message of Job 39 emphasizes trust in God's power and provision in our lives.

hard.title: Job Chapter 39 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Job Chapter 39.

questions.question: What does the horse do in Job 39:21?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is found in Job 39:21, which states that the horse 'paweth in the valley, and rejoiceth in his strength.'

questions.question: How does the horse react to fear according to Job 39:22?
questions.explanation: Job 39:22 describes the horse as one who 'mocketh at fear, and is not affrighted.'

questions.question: What does Job 39:23 mention rattling against the horse?
questions.explanation: In Job 39:23, it states 'The quiver rattleth against him,' referring to the sounds of battle.

questions.question: What does the horse do in response to the trumpet according to Job 39:24?
questions.explanation: Job 39:24 states that the horse 'swalloweth the ground with fierceness and rage,' indicating its aggressive nature.

questions.question: What does the horse smell according to Job 39:25?
questions.explanation: Job 39:25 mentions that the horse 'smelleth the battle afar off,' showing its instinctual awareness of danger.

questions.question: What does the hawk do in Job 39:26?
questions.explanation: Job 39:26 asks, 'Doth the hawk fly by thy wisdom,' indicating the divine wisdom in nature.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'צָפָה' (tsaphah) in Job 39:26 mean?
questions.explanation: 'צָפָה' (tsaphah) means 'to look' or 'to watch,' reflecting the hawk's keen observation in Job 39:26.

questions.question: Which literary device is used in Job 39:19-22?
questions.explanation: Job 39:19-22 employs parallelism, contrasting the horse's strength with its fearlessness, enhancing the text's poetic quality.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of God's creation in Job 39?
questions.explanation: Psalm 104:25-26 reflects on God's creation, similar to Job 39's focus on the natural world and its creatures.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage fulfills the theme of God's control over nature in Job 39?
questions.explanation: Job 38:41 emphasizes God's provision for the creatures, resonating with the themes of Job 39.

questions.question: What comes before Job 39:21?
questions.explanation: Job 39:20 discusses the horse's strength, which directly leads into the description found in Job 39:21.

questions.question: What is the meaning of 'mocketh' in Job 39:22?
questions.explanation: 'Mocketh' in Job 39:22 implies laughter or scorn, as the horse does not fear the sword.

questions.question: The imagery in Job 39:30 conveys what about the eagle?
questions.explanation: Job 39:30 illustrates the eagle's ferocity, as it 'suck up blood' where the slain are, emphasizing its predatory nature.

questions.question: True or False: Job 39 emphasizes God's control over all creatures.
questions.explanation: Job 39 illustrates God's sovereignty over nature and creatures, emphasizing His creative authority.

questions.question: True or False: The unicorn is described as obedient to humans in Job 39.
questions.explanation: Job 39:9-10 indicates that the unicorn is not willing to serve or abide by human commands, demonstrating its wild nature.

theological.title: Job Chapter 39 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Job Chapter 39 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Job 39:5 teach about God's sovereignty?
options: God ordains the freedom and dwelling of wild creatures independently of human control
God limits the freedom of animals to serve human needs exclusively
God is indifferent to the creation of wild animals
God's sovereignty is restricted to human affairs only
questions.correctAnswer: God ordains the freedom and dwelling of wild creatures independently of human control
questions.explanation: Job 39:5 states 'Who hath sent out the wild ass free? or who hath loosed the bands of the wild ass?' indicating God's sovereign role in granting freedom to animals beyond human dominion.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine wisdom and human limitation is taught in Job 39:17?
options: God alone imparts wisdom and understanding; some creatures lack it by divine decree
Human wisdom surpasses that of animals due to natural evolution
All creatures possess equal wisdom given by God
Wisdom is irrelevant to God's creation
questions.correctAnswer: God alone imparts wisdom and understanding; some creatures lack it by divine decree
questions.explanation: Job 39:17 says 'Because God hath deprived her of wisdom, neither hath he imparted to her understanding,' showing that God controls the distribution of wisdom.

questions.question: What doctrine about God's providential care is taught in Job 39:29?
options: God equips creatures with faculties to seek their prey and survive
Creatures act solely by instinct without divine provision
God neglects the daily needs of wild animals
Survival of creatures is random and unguided
questions.correctAnswer: God equips creatures with faculties to seek their prey and survive
questions.explanation: Job 39:29 states 'From thence she seeketh the prey, and her eyes behold afar off,' illustrating God's providential provision enabling creatures to thrive.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Job 39:7 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Job 39:7 says 'He scorneth the multitude of the city, neither regardeth he the crying of the driver,' showing God's sovereign design in the wild ass's independence from human control.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Job 39:26 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Job 39:26 asks 'Doth the hawk fly by thy wisdom?' highlighting God's all-knowing wisdom governing even the flight of birds.

questions.question: How does Job 39:19-25 connect to broader biblical themes about God's power over creation and human warfare?
options: It illustrates God's sovereign control over war and the strength He imparts to creatures
It implies that human strength is independent of divine influence
It teaches that animals are indifferent to human conflict
It suggests that war is a purely human phenomenon without spiritual significance
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates God's sovereign control over war and the strength He imparts to creatures
questions.explanation: These verses describe the horse's strength and fearlessness in battle, reflecting God's providential design, paralleling themes of divine sovereignty over human conflict (Job 39:19-25).

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Job 39:13-18 establish regarding divine wisdom versus human understanding?
options: It prefigures the necessity of divine wisdom for true understanding, fulfilled in Christ
It denies any value to human wisdom in salvation history
It claims that animals possess the highest wisdom
It teaches that human wisdom is self-sufficient for salvation
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures the necessity of divine wisdom for true understanding, fulfilled in Christ
questions.explanation: Verses 13-18 contrast God's gift and withholding of wisdom, pointing toward the biblical theme that true wisdom comes from God alone, fulfilled in Christ (Job 39:13-18).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Job 39:14 and Job 39:16 teach about natural instincts and divine sovereignty?
options: Despite natural instincts, God's sovereignty governs creature behavior including apparent neglect
Animals act purely on instinct without any relation to God's will
God forces animals to act against their nature
questions.correctAnswer: Despite natural instincts, God's sovereignty governs creature behavior including apparent neglect
questions.explanation: Job 39:14 describes the ostrich's neglect of eggs and 39:16 explains this is due to God depriving her of wisdom, showing divine sovereignty over instinctual behavior.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Job 39:1 and Job 39:4 teach about God's providential timing and care in creation?
options: God ordains the seasons and growth cycles for all creatures, independent of human knowledge
God is unaware of the birth timings of animals
Human beings can control animal reproduction fully
Providence does not extend to wild creatures
questions.correctAnswer: God ordains the seasons and growth cycles for all creatures, independent of human knowledge
questions.explanation: Job 39:1 questions human knowledge of birth times and 39:4 describes young animals growing and leaving, indicating God's providential governance over life cycles.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Job 39:9 and Job 39:11 teach about creature subservience and human reliance on strength?
options: Creatures like the unicorn are not made to serve human labor; human reliance on brute strength is limited
All creatures are created for human servitude
Human strength can be fully delegated to animals
Creatures willingly bear human burdens without restraint
questions.correctAnswer: Creatures like the unicorn are not made to serve human labor; human reliance on brute strength is limited
questions.explanation: Verses 9 and 11 ask if the unicorn will serve or be trusted with labor, showing God's design that some creatures are not for human control or reliance.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Job 39:13-18 portrays God as cruel for depriving the ostrich of wisdom. What does this passage actually teach?
options: God sovereignly regulates wisdom distribution as part of creation's order, not cruelty
God is indifferent to the well-being of animals
Animals are morally responsible for their actions
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly regulates wisdom distribution as part of creation's order, not cruelty
questions.explanation: Job 39:17 explains God has 'deprived her of wisdom,' highlighting divine sovereignty in creation design rather than cruelty or moral judgment.

questions.question: What doctrine does Job 39:30 teach about God's provision for even the fiercest creatures?
options: God provides sustenance even for predators, demonstrating comprehensive providence
Predators survive only by chance without God's care
God favors only peaceful creatures with provision
Predators are cursed and neglected by God
questions.correctAnswer: God provides sustenance even for predators, demonstrating comprehensive providence
questions.explanation: Job 39:30 states 'where the slain are, there is she,' showing that God ensures predators receive food, affirming providential care over all creation.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Job 39:6 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Job 39:6 says 'Whose house I have made the wilderness, and the barren land his dwellings,' demonstrating God's sovereign authority over natural habitats.

questions.question: How does Job 39:22-25 contribute to the biblical narrative about fearlessness and divine strength in conflict?
options: It illustrates that God endows creatures with fearless strength, reflecting divine empowerment in conflict
It denies any divine role in conflict
It teaches that fear is absent because of ignorance
It suggests animals are reckless without divine purpose
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates that God endows creatures with fearless strength, reflecting divine empowerment in conflict
questions.explanation: Verses 22-25 depict the horse mocking fear and charging into battle, symbolizing God's provision of strength and courage in adversity (Job 39:22-25).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Job 39:2 and Job 39:3 teach about God's providential timing and the experience of pain in creation?
options: God ordains precise timing of birth and allows pain as part of natural processes
Pain and suffering are accidental and outside God's control
God prevents any form of suffering in creation
Birth timing is random without divine design
questions.correctAnswer: God ordains precise timing of birth and allows pain as part of natural processes
questions.explanation: Verse 2 questions human knowledge of months fulfilled, and verse 3 describes animals 'cast out their sorrows,' indicating God's providential governance including suffering.
